title: LTS branch cut checklist (working notes) — runtime-1.18-lts
body:
Audience: runtime engineers + release eng doing the FIRST LTS branch cut. This is intentionally scrappy. Expect manual steps + gotchas. We’ll convert to a formal runbook once we’ve done 1–2 patch cycles.

Context / scope
- Target: create runtime-1.18-lts release branch from mainline runtime 1.18.x baseline
- Goal: a stable baseline for Dedicated + Private (and later Hosted pinning). Slower-change, monthly patches.
- Non-goal: changing architecture or landing new features into LTS.

Definitions (so we don’t bikeshed mid-cut)
- “Branch cut”: create runtime-1.18-lts branch + tagging conventions + CI wired up so we can build/publish LTS artifacts.
- “Patch”: 1.18.<patch>-lts, e.g., 1.18.1-lts
- “Backport”: cherry-pick of an already-landed mainline PR into runtime-1.18-lts
- “Release gate”: CI + perf-canary + required sign-offs for publishing artifacts and release notes

Pre-branch-cut prerequisites (do these before you click anything)
1) Pick the exact cut commit
   - Decide the baseline SHA on main (pin it; don’t chase). 
   - Criteria: CI green, no open Sev1 incidents, scheduler/kernels in stable configuration.
   - Write down:
     - main SHA
     - runtime version string on main at that SHA
     - any known risks being accepted (e.g., flaky test that’s being waived)

2) Confirm CI + permissions are ready for release branches
   - Verify release-branch workflows exist (or at least branch filters won’t skip jobs).
   - Confirm secrets are available to the release branch context (but NOT overly broad):
     - artifact registry creds
     - signing key access (if we’re enabling on cut)
     - SBOM/provenance tooling access (even if stubbed)
   - If anything is missing, file internal support now (we got blocked last time by permissions/branch protection).
   - Gotcha: release branches sometimes run in a different permission context; jobs that work on main may fail on release/*.

3) Freeze decision: what gets frozen at cut time
   - Kernel autotune defaults: do we freeze now vs first patch?
   - Experimental batching heuristics: should be OFF by default on LTS.
   - Scheduler knobs: keep identical to main unless we have a strong stability reason.
   - Note: If we freeze something, put it in the branch-cut PR so it’s visible/auditable.

4) Perf gate capacity check
   - Confirm we have perf-canary runner availability for the cut window.
   - If the perf fleet is congested, the cut will stall (we should not publish without perf baseline).
   - If needed, coordinate a “perf quiet period” with SRE/infra.

5) Comms prep (internal only)
   - Post in #eng-releases with timeline + who’s release captain.
   - Identify “pagerable” people during cut window:
     - release captain (Connor)
     - CI/build (Sahana)
     - perf suite owner (Marcus)
     - kernel/scheduler approvers (Hiro/Sofia)
     - SRE release readiness (Sean)


Branch cut checklist (the actual steps)
A) Create branch + PR
1) Create the branch
   - Name: runtime-1.18-lts
   - Source: baseline SHA from main
   - Add branch protection rules immediately:
     - require PRs
     - required status checks (CI + perf gate summary)
     - restrict who can push
   - Gotcha: if you create protection rules before checks exist, GitHub UI sometimes won’t let you select them later until first run. Plan for a “seed run”.

2) Open “branch cut” PR (even if small)
   - This is the PR we can point auditors at.
   - Content (ideal):
     - tagging/versioning conventions documented in repo (or release config)
     - disable experimental features not allowed on LTS
     - optional: freeze kernel autotune defaults
   - Reference: GitHub redwood/pr-23184 (if following that approach)

3) Verify version string semantics
   - Ensure builds on runtime-1.18-lts produce a version that includes “-lts”.
   - Decide where the suffix is applied:
     - build metadata vs semantic version tag
   - Confirm with Private installer/Helm folks: they need predictable tags.


B) Wire up CI for release branch
1) Enable/validate release-branch CI workflow
   - Ensure tests run on runtime-1.18-lts:
     - unit + integration
     - scheduler regression suite (if available)
     - build artifacts in staging mode
   - Gotcha: branch filter patterns (e.g., only main) are common.

2) Add/confirm “release branch smoke tests”
   - Specifically for scheduler regressions:
     - mixed prompt lengths
     - backpressure
     - overload/load-shedding
   - If the suite exists but is too slow, at least ensure a minimal subset runs.

3) Seed run to materialize checks
   - Merge the minimal config PR or trigger a workflow_dispatch.
   - This is mainly to:
     - verify secrets work
     - get status checks to show up for branch protection

4) CI gotchas noted from earlier attempts
   - Toolchain mismatch: release branches occasionally build with different runner images than main.
   - Permissions: artifact publish steps might fail due to branch restrictions.
   - “Nightly-only” tests: if required checks are nightlies, the cut will block during business hours.


C) Perf baseline + gating
1) Run perf-canary for release branch
   - Confirm perf-canary workflows target runtime-1.18-lts.
   - Required outputs:
     - p50/p95 latency deltas
     - throughput deltas
     - GPU coverage: at least the enterprise-relevant SKUs
   - Store the perf gate summary artifact somewhere linkable.

2) Decide thresholds + waiver process (if noisy)
   - If perf results are noisy/flaky:
     - rerun first
     - check runner contention
     - only then consider a waiver
   - Waiver must be written down with:
     - reason
     - impact assessment
     - required follow-up

3) Record baseline numbers
   - This doc should contain the baseline for reference, even if approximate:
     - “1.18 main @ SHA X” vs “1.18-lts @ SHA Y”
   - (We can move to a proper sheet later.)


D) Artifact build + provenance (staging first)
1) Build artifacts in “staging” mode
   - Runtime container images
   - Any runtime libs packaged for Private
   - Checksums
   - Provenance metadata
   - SBOM (if available; if not, note the gap + plan)

2) Artifact signing
   - Confirm key access model:
     - who can sign
     - audit trail location
   - Verify signature locally (don’t trust the CI log only)

3) Traceability checklist
   - For each artifact, confirm we can map:
     - artifact digest -> git SHA -> PR list -> release notes
   - Gotcha: if the build pulls dependencies “latest”, reproducibility is broken. Ensure pinned deps.


E) Private installer + Helm sanity
1) Private installer pinning
   - Confirm installer can pin to runtime-1.18.<patch>-lts image tag.
   - Confirm checksum verification step exists and is documented.
   - Verify rollback path: can we go from 1.18.1-lts back to 1.18.0-lts (or previous patch) reliably?

2) Helm chart values
   - Confirm values schema supports selecting LTS channel/tag.
   - Confirm release note URL can be surfaced as an annotation.

3) Compatibility note
   - If any of this requires minimum installer/Helm versions, write it down here now so release notes don’t forget.


F) Release notes scaffolding (even for branch cut)
- We should generate a “branch created” note internally:
  - what SHA we cut from
  - what is frozen/disabled
  - where artifacts will appear
  - how backports are requested


G) Final sign-offs before declaring “branch cut complete”
- Runtime architect sign-off: Noah Patel (sanity on branching + future backports)
- Kernels: Hiro Tanaka (autotune defaults / kernel config)
- Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (scheduler suite green)
- CI/build: Sahana Iyer (reproducible build + secrets)
- Perf: Marcus Reed (baseline + thresholds)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (monitoring readiness for pilot traffic)


Post-cut TODOs (things we always forget)
1) Create GitHub labels + templates
   - backport-candidate
   - lts-approved
   - security
   - release-notes category labels
   - Ensure release notes generator recognizes labels.

2) Backport workflow automation
   - Confirm cherry-pick helper script works on runtime-1.18-lts.
   - Dry-run a trivial backport to validate:
     - conflict detection
     - PR template
     - required reviewers

3) Establish patch cadence calendar
   - Tentative: monthly patch window (week 2) + out-of-band security hotfix
   - Put dates on a calendar and share with Support/CS.

4) Monitoring & dashboards
   - Ensure we can segment LTS traffic/versions.
   - Add alerts for:
     - crash loops
     - latency regression
     - error budget burn


Gotchas (collected during the first cut attempt)
- Branch protection checks don’t show up until you have at least one workflow run on the branch.
- Artifact publish steps can pass but still publish under the wrong tag if the version suffix isn’t wired end-to-end.
- Perf canary variability is worst during shared runner contention; schedule runs during low-traffic hours.
- “Disable experimental batching” must be verified in config AND runtime logs; we had a case where config flag was set but not applied due to environment precedence.
- Kernel autotune default freeze: if we freeze, document how customers override and how we test overrides.
- Private installer needs checksums and a stable URL format; “latest” pointers are not acceptable for regulated customers.


Notes / placeholders (fill during the cut)
- Baseline main SHA:
- LTS branch SHA:
- First successful CI run URL:
- First successful perf-canary summary URL:
- Staging artifact registry path:
- Signing verification notes:
- Any waivers granted:


Quick reference: who to ping for what
- CI/build failures, secrets, runner images: Sahana Iyer
- Perf gate failures, benchmark noise: Marcus Reed (and Allison Grant for signals)
- Kernel behavior/perf variance: Hiro Tanaka
- Scheduler regressions/backpressure: Sofia Ivanova
- Release automation/scripts: Devon Price
- SRE readiness + monitoring: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes


Exit criteria (for “branch cut done”)
- runtime-1.18-lts exists with branch protections
- CI required checks defined + green on branch
- Perf baseline run completed + stored, within thresholds (or waiver documented)
- Artifacts built in staging with checksums/provenance; signature verified
- Private installer + Helm can pin to an LTS-tagged runtime artifact (at least smoke-validated)
- Internal comms posted with links and owners


(End of working notes)
